finding: 71% of routes run into overtime and earn a lower margin.
evidence: Overtime routes margin 4.9% vs 15.9% for the rest; 1935 overtime hours cost about 53,990 in labour.
action: Cap planned stops on routes that regularly exceed planned hours.

finding: Failed deliveries, damage claims and SLA penalties leak money every week.
evidence: Redelivery 15,598 + damage 13,988 + SLA 30,808 = 60,394; average first-attempt success 94.0%.
action: Introduce time-slot booking and pre-delivery notifications on the lanes with the lowest first-attempt rate.

finding: Late routes drive complaints and SLA exposure.
evidence: 697 routes were below 90% on-time; their rating averages 4.22 vs 4.44 elsewhere; SLA penalties total 30,808.
action: Re-sequence stops and tighten delivery windows on the late routes.

finding: 34.7% of routes lose money, wiping out a large part of what profitable routes earn.
evidence: 347 of 1000 routes are loss-making; losses total 24,010 vs net profit 46,054 (7.6% margin).
action: Review the P1/P2 routes in the Action List this week before adding new volume.

finding: Driver labour is the cost line where losing routes overspend most per parcel.
evidence: Losing routes pay 0.48 more per parcel than profitable ones on this line (across 43033 parcels).
action: Set a per-parcel cap on this cost line and track it weekly by depot.

finding: A pre-dispatch model can warn about loss-making routes before they leave the hub.
evidence: Logistic Regression model: test AUC 0.91, recall 93%; the riskiest 20% of routes hold 72% of all losses.
action: Review the highest loss_risk_prob routes each evening before dispatch.

finding: 476 routes leave the hub with vans under 60% full.
evidence: Their margin is 9.5% vs 6.3% for fuller vans.
action: Merge neighbouring light routes or swap to a smaller vehicle type.

finding: The weakest lane is North Hub (cold climate) | Urban Dense.
action: Re-plan or re-price this depot-zone lane first; see its top loss driver in the recommendations.

finding: 50 routes behave unlike the rest of the network.
evidence: Anomalous routes hold 2,494 of losses; most common reason: Complaints per 100 parcels unusually high.
action: Investigate these routes individually in the Anomaly Explorer.

finding: Snow days are the hardest on margin.
evidence: -10.2% margin over 14 routes vs 7.6% network average.
action: Plan lighter routes and add buffer hours when this weather is forecast.

finding: Drivers in the <6 months tenure band earn the lowest margin.
action: Pair drivers in this band with mentors and give them shorter route plans.

finding: Electric Van is the least profitable vehicle type.
evidence: 6.0% margin over 256 routes vs 7.6% network average.
action: Assign this vehicle to better-suited lanes or review its lease terms.
